 Four spots still up for grabs—the race for the ATP Finals is this intense
 Novak Djokovic will have to give it his all to keep his chances alive of winning an eighth title at the ATP Finals.
 Keystone
 With two weeks to go before the start of the ATP Finals in Turin, half of the eight spots in the year-end tournament remain up for grabs. In Basel and Vienna, Alex de Minaur is the only contender to score points.
 Redaktion blue Sport , Keystone-SDA 
 02.11.2026, 15:36 • 02.11.2026, 18:16 Arthur Fils, Rafael Jodar, Novak Djokovic, and Taylor Fritz in Basel; Flavio Cobolli, Frances Tiafoe, Alex de Minaur, and Tommy Paul in Vienna. They all wanted to pick up some more points ahead of this week’s final major Masters 1000 tournament in Paris to gain ground in the race to qualify for the ATP Finals. Except for De Minaur, none of them succeeded.
 With two weeks to go before the year-end tournament featuring the top eight players of the tennis season, only a few participants have been confirmed so far: Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz, Ben Shelton, and Daniil Medvedev. Wimbledon champion Jannik Sinner, who was ranked No. 1 in the world until this Monday, would also have qualified, but he has already had to end his season due to knee problems.
 The decision on the four remaining spots is expected to be made this week in Paris; the winner will earn 1,000 points. As things stand, Cobolli, Fils, Tiafoe, and De Minaur—thanks to his appearance in the Vienna final—would qualify.
 Here's the situation:
 5. Flavio Cobolli (3,690 points): The Italian has the best chances, but he barely scored any points in Vienna. Worse still, the French Open finalist had to retire in tears during his round of 16 match against Matteo Berrettini due to a hip injury.
 6. Arthur Fils (3535): The Frenchman advanced one round at the Swiss Indoors but also had to throw in the towel early against Taylor Fritz. Fils is suffering from back pain and, like Cobolli, is now worried about whether he’ll be able to compete in Paris. At least both players will have a little more time thanks to a bye.
 7. Frances Tiafoe (3390): The American, who has roots in Sierra Leone, drew a tough opponent in Vienna in the resurgent Lorenzo Musetti and was eliminated in the first round.
 8. Rafael Jodar (3234): The young Spanish star was two points away from victory in the Basel round of 16 against the eventual champion, Valentin Vacherot, but lost in the third-set tiebreak. Nevertheless, thanks in part to slip-ups by others, he broke into the top ten of the regular ATP rankings for the first time. The “Rising Star of the Year,” who just turned 20, currently holds the last qualifying spot and won his first-round match in Paris.
 9. Alex de Minaur (3170): The Australian is the big winner of the past week. Thanks to his run to the final in Vienna—including a victory over the new No. 1, Alexander Zverev—he’s back on track. He’ll need to advance one round further than Jodar in Paris, but since he’s (still) ranked higher than Jodar, he’ll benefit from a first-round bye. Last year’s semifinalist could qualify for the ATP Finals for the third consecutive time.
 10. Novak Djokovic (2900): Even the most successful player in tennis history was unable to score as he’d hoped at the Swiss Indoors, suffering a narrow loss in the round of 16 to Jan-Lennard Struff. With seven titles, he is the all-time record holder at the ATP Finals. To keep his chances of winning another title alive, the 39-year-old Serb will have to give it his all. As the No. 10 seed, he won’t benefit from a bye in Paris and will face Basel champion Vacherot right off the bat in the first round. He trails the No. 8 spot by a considerable margin, but should Cobolli and/or Fils be forced to withdraw, the deck will be reshuffled.
 11. Taylor Fritz (2860): The American played well in Basel. However, his semifinal loss to Vacherot prevented him from making a big leap in the rankings. He is currently still entered in Stockholm.
 12. Tommy Paul (2735): The American had the misfortune of facing the eventual champion, Alcaraz, in the quarterfinals in Vienna. He’ll need to pull off an upset in Paris, but faces a tough first-round match against Holger Rune.
 13. Jiri Lehecka (2540): The Czech player now has only a long shot at qualifying. At the Swiss Indoors, he lost his third final of the year, so he was unable to make up enough ground to really close the gap on Turin.
